scope: 1 Peter 3:1-22 source/evidence + final cross-lane integration audit

claims.claim: ὑποτασσόμεναι is a present middle/passive participle, nominative feminine plural.
claims.limitations: Bounded claim only; no downstream inference.

claims.claim: Sarah calling Abraham 'my lord' has a clear Gen 18:12 LXX textual/narrative anchor.
claims.limitations: Bounded claim only; no downstream inference.

claims.claim: Ancient marriage discourse is plural; one uniform Greco-Roman marriage model is unsafe.
claims.limitations: Limited inspection/reconstruction remains; do not promote to settled fact.

claims.claim: The text envisages at least some wives whose husbands disobey the word, not all husbands.
claims.limitations: Limited inspection/reconstruction remains; do not promote to settled fact.

claims.claim: ἀσθενεστέρῳ σκεύει is morphologically clear but its dimension of weakness is exegetically disputed.
claims.limitations: Serious alternatives remain; keep noncompetitive.

claims.claim: The text calls wives co-heirs of the grace of life and commands honor.
claims.limitations: Bounded claim only; no downstream inference.

claims.claim: Accommodation, apologetic, subversive, and mixed household-strategy readings remain debated.
claims.limitations: Serious alternatives remain; keep noncompetitive.

claims.claim: 1 Peter 3:10-12 is a sustained quotation/adaptation of Ps 33:13-17 LXX.
claims.limitations: Bounded claim only; no downstream inference.

claims.claim: Isa 8:12-13 LXX is clearly reused/adapted in 1 Pet 3:14-15.
claims.limitations: Bounded claim only; no downstream inference.

claims.claim: The Isaiah-shaped wording placing Christ with Lord-language is Christologically significant, but the theological formulation is interpretive.
claims.limitations: Limited inspection/reconstruction remains; do not promote to settled fact.

claims.claim: ἁγιάσατε is aorist active imperative 2pl; ἀπολογίαν is accusative singular.
claims.limitations: Bounded claim only; no downstream inference.

claims.claim: Inspected SBLGNT/MorphGNT reads ἔπαθεν ('suffered') in the opening clause, not a verb meaning 'died'.
claims.limitations: Bounded claim only; no downstream inference.

claims.claim: The force of σαρκί ... πνεύματι remains exegetically disputed.
claims.limitations: Serious alternatives remain; keep noncompetitive.

claims.claim: 1 Enoch preserves relevant Watchers confinement/judgment tradition; this is background, not proof of dependence.
claims.limitations: Bounded claim only; no downstream inference.

claims.claim: The identity of the spirits in prison remains contested.
claims.limitations: Serious alternatives remain; keep noncompetitive.

claims.claim: The timing/content of ἐκήρυξεν remains contested among materially different readings.
claims.limitations: Serious alternatives remain; keep noncompetitive.

claims.claim: The text says eight persons were brought safely through water.
claims.limitations: Bounded claim only; no downstream inference.

claims.claim: ἀντίτυπον and βάπτισμα are nominative neuter singular; σῴζει is present active indicative 3sg.
claims.limitations: Bounded claim only; no downstream inference.

claims.claim: ἐπερώτημα is a nominative neuter singular noun; appeal/request, pledge/stipulation and related readings remain live.
claims.limitations: Serious alternatives remain; keep noncompetitive.

claims.claim: 'Baptism now saves you' must be read with the dirt-removal contrast, good-conscience ἐπερώτημα, and resurrection clause.
claims.limitations: Serious alternatives remain; keep noncompetitive.

claims.claim: Christ is in heaven at God's right hand with angels, authorities, and powers subjected to him.
claims.limitations: Bounded claim only; no downstream inference.

claims.claim: 1 Peter directly depends literarily on 1 Enoch's Book of the Watchers.
claims.limitations: Inspected evidence does not warrant this certainty.

claims.claim: ἐπερώτημα lexically means only 'pledge' and therefore cannot mean 'appeal'.
claims.limitations: Inspected evidence does not warrant this certainty.

claims.claim: The SBLGNT Greek opening clause says Christ 'died' for sins.
claims.limitations: Inspected evidence does not warrant this certainty.

do_not_claim: Do not claim every wife in 3:1-6 had an unbelieving husband; the text says some.
Do not make ἀσθενεστέρῳ σκεύει one settled physical/social/moral sense from morphology.
Do not call 3:10-12 mechanically verbatim Psalm 34; use sustained quotation/adaptation.
Do not make morphology prove the full Christological force of Isaiah 8 reuse.
Do not say the inspected SBLGNT opening clause of 3:18 reads 'died'; it reads ἔπαθεν.
Do not settle σαρκί/πνεύματι, spirits in prison, or ἐκήρυξεν chronology from morphology.
Do not claim direct dependence on 1 Enoch from Watchers/Noah parallels alone.
Do not claim ἐπερώτημα means only pledge or only appeal.
Do not prove or disprove baptismal regeneration by lexical fiat.
Do not claim conservative consensus on 3:19-21.
Do not infer empire-wide official persecution from chapter 3 alone.
Do not treat PASS_WITH_HOLD as publication or ranking authorization.

positions: quotation classification and Christological force are interpretive

source_gaps: Critical apparatus remains required before manuscript-distribution claims at 3:18.
Crawford full article remains required before ranking pledge over appeal.
Metadata/bibliographic commentary records remain card-ineligible until relevant passage inspection.
Location-specific Roman/Asia-Minor legal primary evidence remains required before universal wife-status claims.
Direct literary dependence on 1 Enoch remains unproved.

status_policy.VERIFIED: Direct inspected evidence supports the bounded claim.
status_policy.PARTIAL: Useful support exists but part depends on limited inspection/reconstruction.
status_policy.CONTESTED: Materially different serious interpretations remain live.
status_policy.HOLD: Inspected evidence does not warrant publication as fact.
status_policy.REJECTED_OVERCLAIM: The proposed certainty exceeds or contradicts inspected evidence.

A: Mechanical short repeating correct-position pattern (0,1,2,3) resets across pools; option order must be de-periodized and re-audited.
φόβος, adornment norm, Sarah reuse force, κατὰ γνῶσιν, ἀσθενεστέρῳ σκεύει, ὁμοίως, social reconstruction remain noncompetitive even after editorial blocker is fixed.
B: εἰς τοῦτο attachment remains contested; omission motive is unclaimed; broader Psalm role remains scholarly interpretation; Gréaux remains abstract-bounded.
C: Isaiah reuse classification and Christological force remain interpretation; Moyise 2005 is not author-independent from the 2002 coauthored study; metadata-only Jobes/Achtemeier/BDAG remain nonclaim controls.
D: spirits/timing/proclamation, ἐπερώτημα translation, baptism systematics, flesh/spirit force remain disputed/noncompetitive; no production/ranking authorization.
